items.title: Integrating Developmental Neurotoxicity Prediction with Adverse Outcome Pathway Reasoning
items.abstract_or_text: Experimental assessment of developmental neurotoxicity (DNT) is costly, time-consuming, and difficult to scale across large chemical inventories. New approach methodologies (NAMs), including computational approaches based on machine learning, deep learning, and large language models (LLMs), offer new ways to screen and prioritize chemicals. However, these emerging computational approaches have largely focused on predicting toxicity endpoints, with less attention to the mechanisms underlying those predictions. For DNT assessment, understanding this mechanistic basis is equally important. In this study, we integrated LLM inference with the adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework to connect DNT predictions with plausible mechanisms. We constructed an AOP-informed benchmark linking ChEMBL target-activity measurements for 5,861 compounds to 14 AOPs representing five neurodevelopmental outcomes and evaluated ten LLMs for the prediction of molecular initiating events (MIEs), key events (KEs), key event relationships (KERs), and adverse outcomes (AOs), as well as the generation of mechanistic explanations. Explanation quality was evaluated using both a naive LLM judge and a rubric-based LLM judge. Across the zero-shot models, the highest observed macro-F1 scores were 0.818 for MIEs and 0.463 for AOs, but only 0.056 for KEs and 0.034 for KERs, identifying downstream pathway reconstruction as the principal challenge. Few-shot prompting substantially improved performance, with Gemini 3.8 Flash under four-shot prompting achieving macro-F1 scores of 0.956 for AOs, 0.813 for MIEs, 0.492 for KEs, and 0.457 for KERs. Both LLM-judge configurations indicated improved mechanistic explanation quality with few-shot examples, although strong outcome prediction did not consistently ensure recovery of the recorded pathway. Our results demonstrate the potential of AOP-informed LLMs to support DNT assessment by linking predicted neurodevelopmental outcomes to plausible biological mechanisms and enabling predictions to be evaluated at both the outcome and pathway levels.

items.title: Mining the cysteine-motif repertoire of airway mucins reveals redox-active mucolytic peptides
items.abstract_or_text: Muco-obstructive lung diseases are characterized by hyper concentrated airway mucus in which gel-forming mucins form mechanically reinforced polymer networks. Thiol-based mucolytics can reduce disulfide bonds within these networks, but clinically used monothiols show limited potency, whereas stronger reducing agents are constrained by instability and toxicity. Here, we systematically mined the major airway mucins MUC5B and MUC5AC for closely spaced cysteine motifs and screened the resulting mucin-derived peptide library for redox activity, oxidation stability, solubility, epithelial compatibility, and mucolytic activity. The identified Cys–[X]n–Cys peptides displayed pronounced sequence- and pH-dependent thioldisulfide exchange capabilities, with many peptides reacting faster than monothiol controls and several exhibiting reactivity approaching or superior to dithiothreitol (DTT). Reactivity was governed by the combined effects of thiol number, apparent thiol pKa, and local motif architecture rather than by a single physicochemical descriptor. Analysis of free-thiol stability and oxidation products further revealed sequence-dependent access to distinct intra- and intermolecular disulfide states. Together, these measurements provide a systematic sequence-redox framework for understanding how closely spaced cysteine motifs tune thioldisulfide exchange, with implications for the design of redox-active peptides and for understanding how local cysteine sequence environments may contribute to oxidative protein folding. Developability profiling identified soluble, reduced-thiol-stable, and epithelialcompatible candidates. Selected peptides reduced high-molecular-weight MUC5B multimers in cystic fibrosis mucus and MUC5AC multimers in asthma mucus, with activities in the range of DTT and greater than NAC under the tested conditions. These peptides were active in both pathological and healthy mucus, while showing compound-dependent differences in their concentration-response profiles across mucus environments. Our findings point at airway mucins as a source of redox-active peptide candidates with potential for mucolytic therapy and provide a broadly applicable resource for relating cysteine-motif sequence to disulfideexchange behavior.

items.title: A Stereochemical Blueprint for Thermoresponsive Polymers
items.abstract_or_text: Predicting polymer structure-property relationships is challenging due to the vast chemical expanse of polymer design space and the limited availability of high-quality datasets that effectively span the design space. Here, we present a physics-informed framework that integrates high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning to predict the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of stereochemically diverse poly(Nisopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) systems using 5632 MD simulation trajectories, corresponding to a cumulative simulation time of 2816 µs. We use validated MD simulations to generate descriptors that capture local hydration and conformational environments, enabling the extraction of molecular features directly linked to thermoresponsive behaviour. The resulting model accurately reproduces subtle experimentally observed LCST variations arising from changes in tacticity, demonstrating that sequence derived features and simulation-derived hydration descriptors encode the molecular information required to resolve compositiondependent phase behaviour. Beyond LCST prediction, the framework provides mechanistic insight into the molecular origins of thermoresponsive behaviour of PNIPAM, revealing that meso and racemic dyads undergo distinct backbone rotational mediated collapse pathways, with meso dyads requiring backbone rotation through partially hydrated intermediates, whereas racemic dyads collapse within a fixed backbone rotational conformation through closure of the isopropyl-isopropyl distance. These findings establish a transferable simulation-machinelearning strategy for linking polymer structural information to macroscopic properties and accelerating the discovery of functional polymer materials.

items.title: Generating Structural Ensembles of Disordered Proteins with Diffusion Models
items.abstract_or_text: Generative models of protein structures have accelerated scientific discovery. However, the leading structure-prediction models are trained primarily on crystal structures, limiting their ability to sample the conformations of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). All-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can probe the diversity of IDP conformational ensembles, but these simulations are slow and costly. Leveraging the speed of generative models and the accuracy of MD, we develop Zephyr, an SE(3) equivariant diffusion model trained on simulated IDP ensembles. The model generates the structure of a single protein sequence in two phases: a coarse-grained structure is first sampled and heavy atoms are subsequently denoised onto this structure. We evaluate our method on two fronts: ensemble accuracy and sampling efficiency. Across five test systems, the model reproduces key geometric and energetic metrics of the MD ensembles, while sampling at least 63 times faster.

items.title: DeMiR: Density-Matrix-Informed Representations for Molecular Property Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: The Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, which states that all physical quantities in the ground state are functionals of the electron density, suggests that much of a molecule's behavior is encoded in its electronic structure. This study proposes DeMiR, a model that treats electron density matrix prediction as a pretraining task. DeMiR reconstructs cc-pVDZ/B3LYP density matrices for molecules ranging in size from QM9-scale molecules to drug-like molecules with up to 146 atoms, achieving median NMAE values of 1.0% and 2.16%, respectively. At the atomic level, the model's embeddings contain electronic structure information: per-atom electronic observables are predicted with an R² of 0.94 by a linear probe, whereas Uni-Mol reaches 0.84 and a randomly initialized model of the same architecture only 0.63. The embeddings also remove 44.9% of the residual error left by a geometry-based descriptor, showing that this information is not linearly accessible from an explicit geometric descriptor. At the molecular level, transfer depends on the label type. Where electronic structure directly determines the property, transfer holds: on an external experimental pKa test set, fine-tuned DeMiR achieves an MAE of 1.143, significantly outperforming a randomly initialized control with the same architecture and training budget (1.397), and performing on par with or better than chemical foundation models pretrained on far larger datasets. In contrast, for labels such as pIC50 and ADMET, DeMiR shows no consistent advantage over existing general-purpose foundation models, as two-dimensional substructures and physicochemical descriptors have already saturated predictive performance. This study presents the scope within which a connection between electron density prediction capability and molecular property prediction capability holds, along with its boundaries.

items.title: Assessing the state of the art in ADMET prediction: Lessons from the OpenADMET-ExpansionRx community blind challenge
items.abstract_or_text: Computational blind challenges are essential for advancing drug discovery, especially in research areas with limited public data, such as absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity (ADMET) prediction. In this paper, we present the results of our latest community blind challenge, organized in collaboration with Expansion Therapeutics (ExpansionRx). Participants were tasked with predicting nine distinct ADMET endpoints routinely evaluated during lead optimization of compounds in drug discovery programs. Following unprecedented engagement from the global community, this challenge provided valuable insights into the state of the art in machine learning for ADMET modeling. Evaluating submissions against a realistic, challenging dataset from active ExpansionRx drug discovery programs revealed that message-passing neural networks and chemical foundation models dominated among the top performers. Furthermore, the results highlighted the power of proprietary industry datasets and a critical need to optimize predictive workflows for different endpoints independently via multitasking and task-affinity grouping. We also demonstrate how hosting our open-source blind challenge infrastructure on a flexible platform like Hugging Face was pivotal for driving community engagement and visibility. Ultimately, blind challenges supported by robust infrastructure, widespread dissemination, and rigorous post-challenge analysis are fundamental to maximizing the utility of public data releases. We anticipate that these community benchmarks will continue to drive the advancement of ADMET models, enabling their deployment in both early- and late-stage drug discovery.

items.title: Additive Manufacturing of Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) Toward High Performance with AI-Driven Workflows
items.abstract_or_text: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a high-performance fluoropolymer known for its chemical resistance, mechanical strength, thermal stability, and piezoelectric and dielectric behavior, making it an ideal material for additive manufacturing (AM). The first part of this paper provides an overview and demonstration of this potential, with the first section reviewing PVDF materials, crystallographic phases, and fused deposition modeling (FDM) processing. This perspective provides practical guidance for optimizing PVDF AM for engineering applications, as well as the potential for artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) workflows to inform future research.

items.title: Resolving Kinase Resistance Landscapes via Antisymmetric Siamese Graph Networks and Co-Folding Ensembles
items.abstract_or_text: Acquired clinical resistance to small-molecule kinase inhibitors arising from single-point mutations within the ATP-binding cleft presents a critical challenge in precision oncology. Conventional computational modeling relies either on rigid docking—which overlooks induced structural alterations—or computationally demanding alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) methods that cannot scale across wide mutational panels. In this work, we present an end-to-end computational methodology integrating multi-state conformational ensemble generation via the generative biomolecular co-folding engine Boltz with a continuous distance-aware Siamese Graph Neural Network (GNN). Crucially, we introduce an unconstrained bias-free difference head that strictly enforces thermodynamic antisymmetry (f (0) ≡ 0.0 kcal/mol), eliminating trivial baseline drift. Under rigorous 5-fold cross-validation on experimentally characterized kinase resistance pairs, the model achieves an out-of-fold root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 1.637 kcal/mol (MAE = 1.459 kcal/mol, Pearson R = 0.239, Spearman ρ = 0.260). Across a prospective panel of 52 clinical kinase-inhibitor complexes, the architecture structurally rationalizes key resistance patterns, resolving the steric disruption of the ABL1 T315I gatekeeper mutation circumvented by ponatinib and the covalent ablation of EGFR C797S against osimertinib.

items.title: Protein Language Model-Boosted Prediction of Isoelectric Point
items.abstract_or_text: pH plays a key role in many biological processes. When the solution pH equals the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein, the protein carries zero net charge, which minimizes its solubility and thus promotes aggregation. Here we present ESMpI, a sequence-based protein pI predictor that combines optimized pKa values of seven ionizable residue types and two terminals with embeddings from a pre-trained protein language model. Benchmarked against experimental protein pI values, ESMpI outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including structure-based approaches that derive the pI of a protein from residue-specific pKa calculations. Finally, ESMpI requires only sequence information, making it well suited for high-throughput proteomescale analyses and protein engineering.

items.title: Solving density-of-states occupation in disordered systems using neural networks
items.abstract_or_text: Describing density-of-states occupation with high precision in disordered systems is crucial for modeling charge transport and understanding doping mechanisms or interfacial energy-level alignment. Beyond fundamental insight from a mechanistic understanding of these physical phenomena, accurate modeling is pivotal for optimizing technological applications in optoelectronic and thermoelectric devices. However, the required calculations are computationally demanding and inherently complex, preventing systematic computational-experimental approaches. Here, we leverage neural networks to perform these calculations precisely and efficiently. We first demonstrate this approach for the Fermi-Dirac occupation of Gaussian densities of states, achieving accelerations of up to three orders of magnitude, a substantial advantage for advanced modeling workflows that require repeated evaluation of the underlying integrals. We then introduce a neural network for doped molecular materials, such as organic semiconductors, that directly predicts doping levels and Fermi level shifts, circumventing conventional recursive schemes and accelerating computations by nearly five orders of magnitude.

items.title: QMzyme: A Python Package for Automated and Systematic QM-based Enzyme Modeling
items.abstract_or_text: We introduce QMzyme, a Python package to automate the generation of Quantum mechanics (QM)-based enzyme models. QM calculations on enzymes are computationally challenging because full enzyme systems typically contain thousands of atoms, placing accurate QM treatments beyond practical computational limits.Therefore, QM-based enzyme studies rely on identifying a subset of atoms that captures the essential chemistry of the reaction environment, enabling tractable yet chemically meaningful calculations. However, constructing these reduced models requires numerous user-defined decisions, including selection of the starting structure, identification of atoms to include in the QM region, and definition of truncation strategies for QM-only models, all of which can substantially influence the resulting calculations. QMzyme aims to provide the community with a flexible and extensible framework for automated, systematic generation of QM-based enzyme models, enabling researchers to more rigorously evaluate how model construction decisions influence computational outcomes while improving reproducibility and transparency across workflows. By facilitating high-throughput generation and analysis of QM enzyme models, QMzyme supports largescale, data-driven investigations of enzyme structure, function, and reactivity. This effort is especially crucial for the creation of large, chemically consistent datasets that can support emergent artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for accelerated digital discovery in enzymology and biocatalysis.

items.title: From Computation-Ready to Claim-Ready: An Evidence Framework for MOF Machine Learning
items.abstract_or_text: Scientific data are routinely transformed so they can be stored, joined and used by machine-learning models. These steps enable scale, but they can also remove the context that tells us what a prediction means and how far it can be trusted. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) make this problem especially clear: one nominal material may appear as an experimental crystal, an activated simulation structure, a charge-assigned model or a row of descriptors, while information about protonation, counterions, coordination environment or measurement conditions may disappear along the way. We introduce claim readiness: a framework for asking whether the evidence preserved through a data pipeline is sufficient for the scientific claim made at the end of it. By tracing chemical evidence, identifier joins and evaluation choices, we show that data can be highly usable for machine learning yet incomplete for chemistry-sensitive interpretation, and that a model can still be useful for ranking candidates even when its value-level accuracy decreases under a harder split. The wider lesson is not specific to MOFs: trustworthy scientific machine learning requires a traceable connection between the representation used by the model and the evidence needed to support the resulting claim. Highlights • Claim readiness matches scientific claims to evidence preserved in data pipelines • Model-ready materials data can lose chemistry needed for interpretation • Data joins change which materials enter representation comparisons • Harder data splits reduce accuracy while useful candidate ranking can remain

items.title: Consecutive hydrodefluorination for the regioselective synthesis of partially fluorinated arenes
items.abstract_or_text: Fluorinated arenes are critically important motifs in drug discovery, often exhibiting superior bioactivity compared to their non-fluorinated counterparts. While advances in fluorination methods have improved access to monofluoroarenes, the synthesis of di- and trifluoroarenes remains challenging. Here, we present a powerful method for access to partially fluorinated arenes via consecutive hydrodefluorination of perfluoroarenes, executed in one ‘pot’. This method utilises hydridosilicates as the reducing species, which are formed in situ by the combination of phenylsilane and cesium carbonate in dimethylsulfoxide. These conditions avoid precious metal catalysts and exotic reagents, exhibiting exceptional regioselectivity and control over the degree of defluorination. Through an in-depth mechanistic study, we found that hydridosilicates can perform hydrodefluorination by two distinct mechanisms, one thermal and one photochemical. These mechanisms are complementary in substrate scope—together, they enable a method with notable generality.

items.title: Evaluating in-context learning with prompting regimes for transformer-based synthetic health tabular data generation
items.abstract_or_text: Tabular synthetic data generation (SDG) can facilitate research and development in the health domain, as access to health data is restricted. To accommodate for its structural complexity, such as multimodal distributions and fragmentation, transformer models provides an alternative to conventional SDG methods since they are better equipped to infer global spatial coherence due to textual context of tabular records. However, methods for optimising their adaption to tabular SDG are still largely unexplored. We contribute to the understanding of transformer-based SDG by evaluating fidelity and privacy of three prompting regimes, zero shot, one shot and few shot training, for tabular health SDG using small transformer models. We evaluated llama 3.2 (1B and 3B parameters) and Phi (1.3B and 2.7B parameters), on a real clinical dataset. Our results showed that zero shot learning was less prone to hallucinations and performed overall better for fidelity, but at the loss of privacy in comparison to the other regimes. Our results showed no differences between model sizes and families. Future studies should extend the analysis to other models and datasets, and explore strategies to reduce hallucinations.

items.title: Hydrogen-Assisted Reduction of Metal Oxides: Reaction Mechanisms, Process Optimization, and AI/ML-Enabled Pathways for Sustainable Materials Processing
items.abstract_or_text: Hydrogen reduction of metal oxides has been identified as a promising approach for producing some engineering (metallic) materials, both through primary production and the reprocessing of waste materials. Such an approach offers a viable promise for the production of value-added materials in a sustainable manner. Unlike in other reduction processes, where obnoxious gases get 2 released as byproducts, hydrogen reduction, on the other hand, generate water vapor as the clean principal byproduct. Such an approach renders the overall mcheaping process inexpensive because of the use of metal oxides as the cheap feedstocks. However, the manufacturing process offers several challenges, upscaling being one of the major ones. In the present review, an attempt has been made to assess the overall reduction process in an integrated manner, which relates thermodynamic principles, reduction mechanisms, reactor-scale phenomena, and specific application requirements. The principles of thermodynamic constraints related to oxide reducibility are described in relation to the role of reduction temperature, gas compositions, and the gas-solid reaction mechanisms to determine rate-controlling processes, diffusion coefficients, and the role of catalysis for the production of metallic materials by primary manufacturing processes and environmental remediation. There is also the consideration of an enabling role of automation, modeling, and digital twin technologies. The manuscript describes practiced hydrogen reduction processes to produce some of the specific metals, such as iron, nickel, cobalt, and refractory metals, but also the need to improve hydrogen access, efficiency, scalability, and ensure catalyst longevity. Enhanced research in hydrogen, renewable power coupling, AI-assisted process control and reactor design are some of the aspects that have been observed to be the major enablers. The manuscript not only describes the status and future projections but also provides a roadmap for improving the status quo.

items.title: Probing Oxygen Transport in β-Cyclodextrin–Cyclohexane Crystal Nanochannels by Luminescence Quenching from Nanoseconds to Seconds
items.abstract_or_text: Molecular transport in nanochannels can deviate from normal diffusion and exhibit different regimes depending on the observation timescale. However, resolving them from nanoseconds to seconds remains challenging. Here, oxygen transport in β -cyclodextrin–cyclohexane supramolecular crystals containing solvent-filled nanochannels is probed using room-temperature phosphorescence and fluorescence of aromatic luminophores. Their emission lifetimes, ranging from approximately 50 ns to 15 s, provide intrinsic time windows spanning more than eight orders of magnitude. Comparison of fluorescence and phosphorescence quenching for the same guests provides an internal control for probe identity. The effective bimolecular quenching rate constants decrease by approximately five orders of magnitude. Between approximately 50 ns and 10 ms, the dependence follows a power law, k q ∝ τ 0 -0.8 , followed by a nearly lifetime-independent plateau. The theory of diffusion-controlled reactions relates this dependence to the time-dependent oxygen flux and indicates subdiffusive transport at intermediate times with an effective anomalous exponent of approximately 0.4. A random-barrier model with quenched disorder provides a physical interpretation of this regime and its crossover to normal transport at long times. Thus, molecular excited states with different emission lifetimes enable luminescence quenching to resolve distinct temporal regimes of molecular transport under nanoscale confinement.

items.title: Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) Catalysis for Stereoselective Decarboxylative Borylation of Redox-Active Esters
items.abstract_or_text: The Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) is a new class of diboron reagent bearing a borylcatecholato and a boronic acid moiety. Herein, we demonstrate that HACs can also be expontaneously formed in situ from collections of catechols and hypoboric acid. These HACs catalyze the decarboxylative borylation of redox-active esters, providing superior reactivity and selectivity. Equilibrium and kinetic NMR experiments indicate that the catalytic turnover is enabled by the high affinity of catechols for hypoboric acid and their low affinity for boronic acids that is uncovered herein. The catalytic system operates in mild conditions and is robust towards air and moisture, demonstrating its utility in the synthesis of important medicinally-relevant boronates. The enhanced selectivity is sourced in the regioselective radical capture by HAC intermediates at their customized borylcatecholato moiety, which can easily be stereoelectronically tailored for specific applications. These features of the catalytic approach with unsymmetrical HACs presented herein contrast with current state-of-the-art methods based on stoichiometric symmetrical diboron reagents.

items.title: Longitudinal linear-epitope profiling of SLE identifies novel antigens associated with disease and disease activity
items.abstract_or_text: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is the prototypical systemic autoimmune disease defined by the production of autoantibodies directed against diverse self-antigens. Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) are central to SLE diagnosis, and anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies are clinically used to track disease activity. However, these biomarkers provide only partial insight into the full spectrum of autoimmune changes in patients. To expand the known landscape of SLE autoreactivity shared among patients and associated with disease activity, we performed an unbiased characterization of 1,268 SLE plasma samples from 695 SLE patients and 301 healthy controls using phage immunoprecipitation and sequencing (PhIP-seq). This technique preferentially displays linear epitopes, and thus provides a complementary set of autoreactivities to previously discovered autoreactive targets. Despite the marked clinical heterogeneity of SLE, machine learning applied to this data surfaced a shared, reproducible signature that robustly discriminates between SLE and healthy controls in two validation cohorts. Autoreactivities in SLE were significantly enriched for RNA-binding protein targets. Autoreactive proteins containing Basic Acidic Dipeptides (BAD) repeat domains, features associated with biomolecular condensate formation, distinguished patients with high disease activity (by SLEDAI score) from patients with no disease activity. Among all shared autoreactivities, a peptide derived from YTHDF2 emerged as the most prevalent target across SLE cohorts occurring in ~25% of SLE patients and displayed striking sequence similarity to a peptide derived from the Epstein Barr virus (EBV) lytic switch protein BZLF1. Competition assays demonstrated higher-affinity binding to the viral peptide, supporting a model in which antiviral humoral responses to EBV may drive secondary epitope spreading toward molecularly mimicked self-antigens. Remarkably, orthogonal validation using the Luminex bead platform containing a panel of only 10 peptides, including BZLF1, demonstrated strong discrimination between SLE and healthy controls (AUC = 0.95). Together, these findings identify a rich, greatly expanded landscape of autoreactivities in SLE, candidate biomarkers associated with high disease activity, and provide mechanistic insight linking EBV-driven immunity to epitope-specific autoimmunity in lupus.

items.title: Heterotypic Condensate Formation by Prion Proteins and Pro-Inflammatory S100A9
items.abstract_or_text: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of biomacromolecules has been shown to influence a large variety of biological processes via the formation of membraneless organelles. Aberrant LLPS, however, has been implicated in a number of oncological and neurodegenerative disorders. Proteins related to Alzheimer's, Parkinson's diseases and other major amyloidoses have all been shown to form these condensates. Interestingly, some amyloidogenic proteins were demonstrated to form heterotypic droplets, where both molecules coexisted within the same condensate and affected each other's aggregation. While such cross-interactions have been reported numerous times under non-LLPS conditions, the heterotypic droplet assemblies were only shown for a very limited number of amyloidogenic proteins. In this work, we examine heterotypic LLPS of prion proteins and the pro-inflammatory S100A9, whose cross-interaction under non-LLPS conditions we confirmed in a previous work. The results show that this interaction under condensation-promoting conditions enhances their aggregation, leading to the formation of a higher concentration of amyloid structures. These findings suggest that the pro-inflammatory S100A9 may have a critical role in promoting prion protein aggregation via the assembly of heterotypic condensates under high molecular crowding conditions.

items.title: Overcoming the Density Limitation of Polyhydroxyurethane Self-Blown Foams through Sol–Gel Chemistry
items.abstract_or_text: Non-isocyanate polyurethane foams (NIPUFs), particularly polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams prepared by cyclic carbonate aminolysis, are promising safer alternatives to conventional polyurethane foams. Although water-induced CO 2 self-blowing can now be achieved from room-temperature formulations within minutes, access to foams with densities below 150 kg·m -3 remains a significant challenge. Herein, we introduce alkoxysilanes as additives for the fabrication of NIPUFs with ultra-low densities (30–50 kg·m -3 ). The strategy synergistically combines CO 2 generation from cyclic carbonate hydrolysis with in situ alcohol formation through alkoxysilane hydrolysis and condensation. Without external physical blowing agents, surfactants, or foam stabilizers, hybrid foams with densities of 28–35 kg·m -3 were obtained, entering the range of conventional lightweight foams. The resulting open-cell foams showed high porosity, complete cyclic carbonate conversion, and tunable mechanical properties depending on amine structure. Their rebound resilience was also strongly and reversibly modulated by humidity, increasing from 0–9% in the dry state to 37–56% at 90% RH and recovering upon drying. This work demonstrates a simple and versatile alkoxysilane-assisted self-co-blowing strategy toward low-density NIPU cellular materials with humidity-responsive mechanical functionality.

items.title: Electrochemically Controlled Crystallization Using Selective Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis
items.abstract_or_text: Nitrogen and phosphorus nutrient recovery from wastewater represents a critical frontier for circular fertilizer manufacturing and effective water treatment. Conventional chemical precipitation remains hindered by the need for expensive reagent consumables. Here, we examine an integrated, chemical-free electrochemical mixer (ECM) system that leverages selective bipolar membrane electrodialysis (SBED) to achieve precise struvite (MgNH4PO4 · 6H2O) crystallization. We furthermore demonstrate how control over current density (1–5 mA cm−2), specific charge loading (20–40 C m−3), and hydraulic retention time (τ = 2.3–6.9 s) enhances downstream crystallization yield, purity, and morphology. Shortening retention promotes boundary-layer convection, reducing in-cell scaling energy penalty (∆E) by 86% and total stack energy consumption by 22%. Operating within an optimized pH window (7.7 97%), bypassing competitive newberyite crystallization. We unify the ECM transport kinetics and crystallization thermodynamics into a single dimensionless descriptor—the crystallization index—which establishes a linear correlation to predict the product yield based on upstream transport dynamics. Steady specific energy consumption of 9.38 ± 0.9 kWh kg−1 − struvite through autonomous in-situ acid flushing confirms system stability with minimal scaling. Finally, techno-economic analysis evaluates the levelized cost of struvite produced as 996 t−1, which is a reduction in operating expenditures by a maximum of 89% compared to commercial phosphorus recovery installations. Ultimately, the ECM eliminates crystallization chemical dependencies and reduces membrane scaling bottlenecks, establishing a highly tunable and efficient separations reactor with precise control of crystal products.

items.title: State-selective nanobodies to probe Guanylate-binding protein coat assembly and function
items.abstract_or_text: Cell-autonomous immunity against gram-negative bacterial pathogens relies on Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs). GBPs are interferon-inducible guanosine triphosphate hydrolases that coat cytosolic bacteria and promote non-canonical inflammasome activation. GBP coat assembly is initiated by GBP1, which binds bacterial lipopolysaccharide and recruits further paralogs in a hierarchical and nucleotide-dependent manner. Dissecting the contributions of individual GBPs has remained challenging because the seven human paralogs are structurally similar and undergo nucleotide-driven conformational changes that are difficult to resolve in cellular and biochemical experiments. Here, we developed a nanobody toolbox for the state-selective probing of human GBP coat assembly. We identify eight nanobodies with distinct paralog, domain, and conformational specificities and define their binding profiles and epitopes using complementary biophysical assays and cryogenic electron microscopy. We further demonstrate the utility of selected nanobodies by demonstrating their functionality in membrane reconstitution assays and in infected cells. A dimer-disrupting nanobody blocks progression of GBP-coat assembly from soluble GBP1 assemblies to LPS-associated coats, suggesting a stage-specific structural transition during coat formation. In contrast, a dimer selective nanobody binds assembled coats without measurably perturbing their organisation and is robustly recruited to GBP1-positive bacteria in infected cells, indicating that this dimer interface remains intact and accessible in coat-associated GBP1. Together, these nanobodies establish a set of state-selective reagents to distinguish, perturb, and probe GBP assemblies in structural, biochemical, and cellular studies

items.title: Answering clinicians' questions over trial evidence tables with verifiable, feedback-driven language models
items.abstract_or_text: Systematic reviews condense clinical trials into evidence tables, yet clinicians can interrogate these tables only through database queries, and many questions concern attributes that the table does not record, such as a drug's target class or a harmonised endpoint. Here we introduce FD-SCoPE, a language-model framework that answers both kinds of question, exposes the query, the selected trials and the derivation rule behind every answer, and learns from expert corrections. On an oncology evidence table of 159 immune checkpoint inhibitor trial records, FD-SCoPE completed all 140 clinician-style tasks (alternatives, 90.7--97.9%). For questions needing derived attributes it retrieved 99.3% of relevant trial records at a positive predictive value of 89.8% and outperformed four alternative approaches (derived-value F1 77.7% versus 64.8--73.4%). Corrections on 299 questions, simulated from reference answers, raised F1 on 1,201 unseen questions from 77.9% to 84.9%. Language models coupled with executable queries, verified programs and expert feedback can give clinicians auditable access to trial evidence.

items.title: Polyglutamine aggregation proceeds by stochastic nucleation in the C. elegans nervous system
items.abstract_or_text: Fibrillar protein aggregation is the hallmark of a wide variety of neurodegenerative diseases. It is still poorly understood how soluble proteins transition to fibrillar aggregates, in particular within the complex environment of cells and tissues. Here, we employ the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of polyglutamine aggregation in the nervous system of a multicellular animal. By using fluorescence microscopy in combination with mathematical modelling, we find that polyglutamine aggregation occurs by stochastic nucleation in individual neurons, at a rate that is of the same order of magnitude as previously determined for muscle cells. The J-protein DNAJB6 strongly suppresses polyglutamine aggregation in both tissues, consistent with a mechanism in which aggregation is limited by primary nucleation. We confirm that the same mechanism holds true for a construct including the disease-relevant flanking regions of Huntingtin exon 1. Altogether, our data reveal that polyglutamine aggregation occurs spontaneously and largely independent of the cellular context.

items.title: DNA binders based on the integration of duocarmycins into minor groove-targeting polyamides have potent and selective anti-trypansosomal activity
items.abstract_or_text: Duocarmycins are attractive DNA alkylating agents due to their high potency; however, increasing their selectivity has always been a challenge. Here, we describe the integration of the duocarmycin subunits DSA and CI into minor groove-targeting polyamides, compounds that can ‘read’ DNA sequences. The synthesis of a CI analogue suitably substituted for solid phase synthesis using Fmoc-chemistry is described. The synthesis of the hybrid compounds is achieved using solid phase methods on chloro-trityl resin. The resulting hybrids display sequence-selective DNA alkylation, depending on the enantiomer and position of the duocarmycin unit as might be expected, except for the compounds with a central DSA alkylation subunit, which act more similarly to reversed analogues. The CI hybrids with a central unit are relatively unreactive with DNA and modelling studies suggest that the CI subunit is sub-optimally located for alkylation in these structures. Investigations against the parasite T. brucei, responsible for African trypanomiasis, highlight compounds with nanomolar potency and high selectivity (SI >300), showing that the integration of duocarmycins into the backbone of polyamides has promise for developing gene-targeting small molecule anti-parasitic agents.

items.title: pH-responsive nanopores enable programmable transmembrane potential
items.abstract_or_text: Biological ion channels achieve highly selective, ultrafast ion transport through stimulus-responsive gating, in which conformational changes triggered by chemical cues such as pH that modulate channel permeability with exquisite precision. Replicating this coupled chemical-structural functionality in synthetic membranes remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for scalable platforms relevant to energy harvesting, desalination, and chemical sensing. Here, we report a bioinspired polymer-metal-organic framework (MOF) composite membrane in which an amino acid (histidine) functionalized MOF nanopores serve as synthetic proton-gated anion channel. The histidine modified, spatially confined ion transport pathway exhibited selective Cl- diffusion at pH 4, enabling pH programmable control of transmembrane potential. Micrometer-scale percolated transport networks within the composite membrane, architecturally inspired by ion channels embedded in lipid bilayers, translate localized αNH2(histidine)-anion specific interaction into macroscopic, anion selective transmembrane potential output. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for coupling chemical gating with macroscopic ion transport in synthetic membrane systems, with direct implications for ion separations, sensing and osmotic energy generation.

items.title: Preoptic transcriptomes during courtship reveal the molecular basis of behavioral coordination in a highly social cichlid
items.abstract_or_text: Human and non-human animals often coordinate their behavior, a phenomenon thought to strengthen relationships by enabling sequential assessment of an interaction partners quality as a mate or rival, a process that directly affects evolutionary fitness. There is increasing evidence that behavioral coordination is reflected by synchronized neural activity of the on interacting partners, though few studies have examined synchronization at the level of gene expression. Here, we use Burtons Mouthbrooder cichlid, Astatotilapia burtoni, to examine how neural transcriptomes are synchronized while male-female pairs engaged in variable amounts of reproductive behavior. A. burtoni females naturally display highly coordinated reproductive behavior with a male partner only directly prior to spawning, yet this behavior can be experimentally induced with exogenous prostaglandin F2 alpha (PGF2a), which also acts by releasing pheromones to promote male courtship behavior. We quantified reproductive behavior and circulating sex steroid hormones of PGF2a-treated pairs. We then used transcriptome analysis of the preoptic area - a key node in the regulation of reproductive behavior across vertebrates - and identified gene co-expression modules that showed sex-specific activity in modulating reproductive behavior. Our results, which implement a novel approach to measure transcriptome synchronization, demonstrate a remarkable degree of male-female POA transcriptome synchronization that depends largely on the reproductive responsiveness of the female, mirroring how natural reproduction is driven by female behavior. Together, our work advances our understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which interacting individuals align their actions and how they experience social interaction.

items.title: Comparison of sodium azide- and cooling-based immobilization methods for Caenorhabditis elegans chemotaxis assays
items.abstract_or_text: Chemotaxis assays are widely used to quantify sensory-driven behavioral responses in Caenorhabditis elegans. Sodium azide is commonly used to immobilize animals at assay endpoints, although concerns have been raised that diffusion beyond the endpoint region could affect behavior before a choice is completed. We compared sodium azide-mediated immobilization with post-assay cooling using the repellent 1-octanol and attractant diacetyl. Wild-type animals showed robust avoidance of 30% 1-octanol and attraction to 0.5% diacetyl with either method, across multiple assay durations, and with or without worm food Escherichia coli OP50. These results support post-assay cooling as an alternative endpoint-scoring method.

items.title: EndoMT: An R Package Resource for Endothelial-Mesenchymal Transition Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Introduction: Endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) is a dynamic endothelial cell-state transition increasingly implicated in fibrosis, vascular dysfunction, inflammation and cancer. Despite expansion of EndoMT-focused transcriptomic research, EndoMT representation remains limited to broader epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) frameworks in standard gene set repositories. Methods: To address the absence of a general-purpose EndoMT gene set for transcriptomic enrichment analysis, we developed an open EndoMT gene set resource and accompanying R package. A literature-informed EndoMT gene set was curated and directionally assigned to EndoMT UP and EndoMT DOWN signatures according to reported or hypothesised expression during partial EndoMT, defined here as an active transitional state rather than a complete mesenchymal endpoint, to improve capture of EndoMT-associated transcriptional changes across different stages of the process. Genes were annotated by marker subtype and implemented as Gene Matrix Transposed files distributed through the R package, together with exported R objects and gene-level metadata. Benchmarking was performed using bulk RNA-seq data sets GSE118446, comprising seven-day IL-1l{beta}/TGF-{beta}2-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and human pulmonary arterial endothelial cells, and GSE342578, comprising three-day TGF-{beta}1/2/3-treated HUVECs; single-cell RNA-seq data set GSE237895, comprising seven-day TGF-{beta}1-treated and SNAI1-overexpressing HUVECs; and endothelial cell and cancer-associated fibroblast populations from human metastatic melanoma single-cell RNA-seq data set GSE72056. Results: In GSE118446, EndoMT UP was positively enriched and EndoMT DOWN negatively enriched in chronically IL-1{beta}/TGF-{beta}2-treated endothelial cells, concordant with experimentally validated EndoMT induction, while partial EndoMT-associated enrichment was detected in single ligand-treatment. In contrast, EndoMT UP was negatively enriched following acute TGF-{beta}1/2/3 treatment, suggesting temporal differences between acute TGF-{beta} stimulation and chronic EndoMT induction. In GSE237895 mesenchymal-like endothelial cells, EndoMT UP was positively enriched and EndoMT DOWN negatively enriched in both TGF-{beta}1-treated and SNAI1-overexpressing models. EndoMT gene sets also discriminated endothelial and mesenchymal/stromal transcriptional states in GSE72056 metastatic melanoma. Marker subtype and Gene Ontology Biological Process analyses provided additional exploratory resolution of EndoMT-associated components beyond MSigDB Hallmark EMT. Discussion: The EndoMT R package provides a dedicated, accessible and interoperable resource for EndoMT-focused transcriptomic enrichment analysis. Benchmarking demonstrates utility for detecting established, partial and divergent EndoMT-associated states, supporting broad applicability across EndoMT biology research.

items.title: Communication as a Two-Person Neural Process: fNIRS Hyperscanning in Adults with and without Post-Stroke Aphasia
items.abstract_or_text: Communication is inherently interactive, yet most neuroimaging studies examine individuals in isolation. Here, we used functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) hyperscanning to investigate interbrain synchrony (IBS) during naturalistic communication. In Study 1, 13 healthy familiar dyads completed Joint Singing, Joint Reading, and Picture Guessing tasks. IBS was quantified using wavelet transform coherence across bilateral frontal and temporoparietal regions. Joint Singing produced higher IBS than the other tasks in several regions, including the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and temporoparietal junction, and selected effects were greater in true than pseudo-dyads. In Study 2, we applied the same paradigm to five individuals with chronic post-stroke aphasia interacting with trained speech-language pathologists. IBS could be estimated in all dyads after lesion-informed channel exclusion, although regional coverage varied with lesion location. These findings demonstrate that fNIRS hyperscanning can capture task-dependent interpersonal neural coupling during spoken interaction and can be extended to communication involving individuals with aphasia. This approach provides a foundation for studying how neural coordination between communication partners relates to functional communication and partner-supported interaction.

items.title: No Evidence of tACS-Primed Enhancement of Alpha Neurofeedback
items.abstract_or_text: Neurofeedback shows promise as a clinical intervention, but its effectiveness is hindered by variability of response across individuals. One factor influencing neurofeedback success may be endogenous brain states, particularly the baseline power within target frequency bands. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) provides a potential mechanism to modulate these baseline frequency bands. This study explored whether tACS could effectively enhance participants' ability to gain neurofeedback control by increasing lateralised posterior alpha activity prior to engagement in a covert spatial attention-based neurofeedback task. Participants completed three counterbalanced sessions: 1) alpha tACS and active neurofeedback, 2) alpha tACS and sham neurofeedback, 3) gamma (40Hz) tACS and active neurofeedback. Neurofeedback performance was assessed via lateralised posterior alpha power shifts and Posner task reaction times. We identified no difference in reaction times or lateralised alpha power shifts across conditions. While participants reliably demonstrated lateralised posterior alpha patterns, consistent with the covert spatial attention neurofeedback protocol, no advantage of active neurofeedback over sham was observed. The lack of significant effects underscores the need for further rigorous tACS studies to identify the parameters essential for successful neural entrainment, and to evaluate its potential in enhancing neurofeedback efficacy.

items.title: High-Throughput Morphological Profiling of Patient-Derived Human Liver Organoids for Hepatotoxicity Hazard Identification and Compound Prioritization
items.abstract_or_text: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a major challenge in drug development because existing in vitro models poorly predict clinical hepatotoxicity. We coupled patient-derived human liver organoids (HLOs) with high-content imaging and automated machine learning (ML) to detect hepatotoxicity-associated phenotypes by morphological profiling. HLOs from six DILI patients and one healthy donor (n = 7) retained donor-specific baseline phenotypes in hepatocyte maturity, metabolism, and morphology. ML models trained per line on MAD-robustized, well-level-aggregated median features achieved compound-level AUROCs of 0.88 (95% CI 0.86-0.90) to 0.91 (95% CI 0.89-0.93) and balanced accuracies of 0.81-0.84 in distinguishing 54 hepatotoxicants from 20 non-hepatotoxic controls. Averaging predictions across all seven lines at an optimized threshold gave 94.4% sensitivity (95% CI 84.6-98.8%) and 85.0% specificity (95% CI 62.1-96.8%), substantially outperforming HLO cytotoxicity assays and cancer cell line profiling. Lines were moderately-to-highly concordant (Pearson r = 0.66-0.85), and benchmark concentration modeling revealed reproducible inter-line differences in phenotypic sensitivity (median 4.0-fold, several compounds exceeding 20-fold). Exposure anchoring of benchmark concentrations to human-equivalent plasma concentrations, using in vitro mass-balance dosimetry and curated plasma free fractions, placed organoid points of departure within 100-fold of clinical Cmax for 60 of 66 compounds (23-fold residual offset, 95% CI 12-45), and placed two of the three misclassified negative controls an order of magnitude above clinical Cmax. Sulindac injury signatures were significantly enhanced by TNF co-treatment, demonstrating capacity to detect pro-inflammatory-mediated DILI. This platform preserves inter-line variability while enabling reproducible, scalable multi-line consensus hazard classification; because compounds were tested over a common nominal concentration range, the readout defines hepatocellular hazard, which must be combined with exposure as an independent input to estimate clinical DILI risk.

items.title: Metabolic rewiring induces a viral mimicry-mediated quiescence in glioblastoma
items.abstract_or_text: Glioblastoma is a highly aggressive brain tumour driven by therapy-resistant glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) that switch between dormant and proliferative states through poorly defined programs. In this study, we identify SAT1, encoding the rate-limiting polyamine-catabolic enzyme SSAT1, as enriched in quiescent GSCs, linking metabolic rewiring to dormancy. Pharmacologic induction of SSAT1 with the polyamine analogue N1,N11-Diethylnorspermine (DENSpm) triggers a chemoprotective, reversible growth arrest in patient-derived GSCs, independent of stemness, differentiation or senescence. SAT1-induced dormancy coincides with reduced eIF5A hypusination and global protein translation, and a marked rise in double-stranded RNA that activates type I interferon signalling. Knocking down the mitochondrial antiviral-signalling protein, essential for antiviral innate immunity, partially reverses this growth arrest, establishing viral mimicry as functionally required for dormancy. Single-cell and cohort analyses across GSCs and neural stem cells demonstrate that susceptibility to metabolically induced quiescence is set by an intrinsic inflammatory tone and lysosomal dependency, defining a context-dependent metabolic-immune axis which can be targeted to prevent GBM progression.

items.title: Glycosaminoglycan presentation-dependent regulation of glial responses by Orion during Drosophila neuronal pruning
items.abstract_or_text: Neuronal pruning refines neural circuits by eliminating unnecessary connections to ensure proper nervous system function. In Drosophila mushroom body gamma-neuron remodeling, the chemokine-like protein Orion is required for astrocyte infiltration and phagocytosis. This study investigated whether glial responses depend on how Orion is presented. We found that Orion interacts with glycosaminoglycans (GAG) associated to proteoglycans, which are essential for proper axon pruning. Tethering Orion to the gamma-neuron plasma membrane, mimicking glycosaminoglycan binding, was sufficient to induce astrocyte infiltration into axon bundles. However, membrane-bound Orion alone could not efficiently support phagocytosis, which additionally requires a soluble and mobile Orion pool. We also identified exosomes carrying GAG-bound Orion as potential mediators of neuronal remodeling. These findings provide the first evidence that glial infiltration can be uncoupled from phagocytosis, demonstrating that the mode of Orion presentation regulates distinct glial mechanisms during neuronal remodeling.

items.title: Early-life adversity alters the adult blood proteome primarily in female mice
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Early-life adversity (ELA) is one of the strongest predictors of poor mental and physical health later in life, increasing an individual's risk for disorders ranging from depression to metabolic syndrome. However, whether and how ELA shapes immune memory through adulthood, subsequently affecting susceptibility to immune-associated diseases such as autoimmunity, remains elusive. Methods: To address this question, we employed a translationally and ethologically relevant mouse model of resource deprivation, the limited bedding and nesting model, to study the long-term effects of ELA on the immune system. ELA was induced by limited bedding and nesting material in the cage during postnatal days (P)2-9, which provokes fragmented and unpredictable maternal behavior in the dams, and results in chronic stress in the pups. Nucleic acid Linked ImmunoSandwich Assay (NULISA) was used to survey the proteome of adult (~P90) mice of both sexes that experienced ELA vs. control conditions. Results: Using a novel proteomic method, we detected significant upregulation in the levels of IL-17A in the adult blood, primarily in females. Within females, ELA also upregulated IL-13 and CCL3. Three proteins, HGF, PDGFA, and WNT16, were significantly downregulated in ELA mice of both sexes. Conclusions: Being a hallmark proinflammatory cytokine, IL-17A is found to increase in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), as well as in animals with lupus-like diseases in virtually all reports. Importantly, autoimmune diseases like SLE have a higher prevalence in women than men, and our data support this sex bias. Together, our data suggest that ELA shapes long-term immune function in a way that may increase risk for autoimmune diseases, with promise for the development of more targeted and personalized therapies for autoimmunity.

items.title: Verification Debt in Automated Biological Research Workflows: A Proof-of-Concept
items.abstract_or_text: Recent biological research has shown significant interest and progress towards adoption of agentic AI systems. Domain specific agentic platforms with access to large collections of biological tools with code generation and/or querying capabilities, such as Biomni (illustrative case in point), are representative of the capability to orchestrate automated research workflows. Such platforms enable collaborative AI workspace for drug discovery, genomics, bioinformatics, literature research, and experimental planning for biologists and researchers. When such platforms are used for the aforementioned workflows, individually validating every agentic decision and the research process by which it was reached becomes challenging due to the scale of decisions involved and oftentimes, insufficient disclosure of assumptions and methodological choices, limited traceability of evidence, and interpretive judgments embedded throughout the workflow, giving rise to verification debt. Verification debt in agentic environments could result in unexpected failures and consequences in downstream experiments. This study focuses on empirical qualitative characterization of verification debt in agentic (prompt to outcomes) workflows. Biomni was chosen the testing AI agentic platform in this study mainly due to the descriptive traces it provides to track every agentic step. Verification debt is examined through two complementary angles: the individual agentic decision steps that carry claims and evidence, and the underlying research process by which the agent arrives at and reports them. This study attempts to characterize verification debt with 10 test cases (covering proteomics, genomics and drug discovery) with varying degree of biological nuance across three identical and independent runs. Verification debt is represented through 9 decision-step metrics and 13 research-process metrics, and also propose the VERIFY framework for evaluating scientific verifiability and validity in agentic workflows.

items.title: A two-step organoid screen identifies transient p53 activation as a senolytic strategy for radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction
items.abstract_or_text: Radiotherapy significantly improves the survival of head and neck cancer patients. However, it frequently damages the salivary glands, causing persistent hyposalivation and xerostomia. Radiation-induced cellular senescence within the salivary gland stem/progenitor cell niche contributes to hyposalivation, suggesting that selective elimination of senescent cells could promote tissue recovery. However, the effectiveness of senolytic compounds is strongly context dependent, varying with tissue of origin and potentially impairing regenerative cells required for functional restoration. Here, we developed a two-step organoid-based screening methodology that integrates the preferential induction of apoptosis in irradiated, senescence enriched, salivary gland organoids with the preservation of stem/progenitor cell regenerative capacity. As a first step, the senolytic activity of candidate drugs was tested to identify drugs that induced apoptosis in senescent cells of irradiated organoids but were not or less toxic to unirradiated organoids. As a second step, the confirmed senolytic compounds were tested for effects on stem cell self-renewal potential. Using this approach, we identified Nutlin3a, an MDM2 inhibitor and p53 activator, as the compound with the most favorable toxicity profile in salivary glands. Last, we confirmed the anti-senescence and pro-regenerative potential of Nutlin3a in an in vivo mouse model of radiation-induced hyposalivation, where localized Nutlin3a delivery resulted in a robust increase in saliva production, as early as two weeks after administration. These findings establish an organoid-based strategy for identifying tissue-adapted senolytic interventions and propose transient local p53 activation with Nutlin3a as a potential approach to mitigate radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction.

items.title: Magnetic Field Enhanced Docosahexaenoic Acid Delivery for Acetylcholine Restoration in Alzheimers Disease an In Silico Study
items.abstract_or_text: Alzheimers Disease (AD) is characterised by the progressive depletion of Acetylcholine (ACh), a neurotransmitter essential for cognition and synaptic communication. Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the predominant omega 3 polyunsaturated fatty acid in neuronal membranes, raises cerebral ACh and supports cholinergic transmission, but its therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor blood brain barrier permeability and slow passive diffusion. This work addresses these limitations through a closed form mathematical model coupling the spatiotemporal dynamics of DHA diffusion and ACh synthesis under an externally applied static magnetic field. Because DHA is diamagnetically anisotropic, it aligns along the field axis through diamagnetic torque while body cells form field aligned linear arrays; together these effects raise the effective diffusion coefficient of DHA. At a representative observation point, 0.5cm, magnetic field assisted transport reduces the time for ACh to reach a therapeutic threshold by 83.3%, from 10.55 s to 1.76 s. This reduction is spatially uniform across the modelled range of 0 to 3.0 cm from the source, with the absolute saving growing from 6.71 s at the source to 19.21 s at 3.0 cm. Co-evolution analysis reveals the mechanism: by the end of a 2.0 s window the field elevates DHA 7.39 fold relative to baseline, driving ACh to 133.7% of threshold versus only 18.1% without the field. A Brain Computer Interface (BCI)-based closed loop dosing framework is additionally proposed for future clinical validation. These findings establish a quantitatively grounded theoretical basis for magnetically enhanced DHA therapy as an approach to cholinergic restoration in AD.

items.title: KSHV upregulates the long non-coding RNA PURPL via p73 to suppress p53
items.abstract_or_text: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are a class of regulatory RNAs with lengths exceeding 200 nucleotides. The lncRNA PURPL (p53 upregulated regulator of p53 levels) is a p53-regulated gene. PURPL is an oncogenic lncRNA that represses p53 function; it is upregulated in many tumors and promotes cancer cell proliferation. Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) is the causative agent of all forms of Kaposi sarcoma (KS) and is tightly associated with primary effusion lymphoma (PEL). We found upregulation of PURPL in both de novo and chronically KSHV-infected cells. We found that p73 (a p53 homolog) associates with the PURPL promoter and upregulates PURPL expression. Previously, it has been shown that KSHV-encoded latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA) stabilizes p73. We found that ectopic expression of LANA increased both p73 protein levels and PURPL expression. p73 knockdown abrogates PURPL upregulation following KSHV infection. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASO) targeting PURPL reduced PEL cell proliferation and increased acetylated p53 levels. In contrast to p53, p73 is not repressed by PURPL RNA. In summary, our study reveals how an oncogenic virus can utilize p73 to upregulate the oncogenic lncRNA PURPL as an additional way to repress p53. Moreover, we propose another mechanism by which p73 may promote tumor growth.

items.title: Templated paired helical filament formation and tau fold-dependent inclusion morphologies in primary neurons
items.abstract_or_text: Neurodegenerative tauopathies are characterized by the abnormal assembly of tau into amyloid filaments with distinct, disease-specific folds. These filaments are proposed to spread in a prion-like manner, thus underlying the progression of pathology in diseased brains. A prediction of this hypothesis is that tau filaments will induce progeny filaments identical to the input seed material, yet cellular models of templated tau assembly have failed to fully recapitulate brain-derived filament structures. Here, we show that mixed primary mouse cortical neurons overexpressing full-length human tau via adeno-associated virus transduction propagate Alzheimer's disease paired helical filaments upon exposure to human brain-derived seeds. Using minimal tags and core mutations, we were able to unambiguously differentiate induced aggregates from the original seeds. Super-resolution microscopy and live-cell imaging revealed progressive inclusion formation in neurons. Moreover, seeding primary neurons with brain extracts from individuals with Pick's disease, corticobasal degeneration and progressive supranuclear palsy induced the formation of morphologically distinct inclusions. Together, these findings establish that primary neurons provide an environment for the faithful propagation of paired helical filaments and show that tau filament folds dictate higher-order inclusion morphologies within neurons.

items.title: Perceptual sensitivity is explained by optimization for ecological tasks
items.abstract_or_text: When asked to discriminate between two stimuli that differ along some dimension, such as intensity, frequency, or orientation, humans exhibit a smallest stimulus difference, or threshold, below which discrimination becomes impossible. These limits on perceptual sensitivity have traditionally been explained by internal noise. Contemporary theories instead link perceptual sensitivity to efficient coding of the natural environment but have not been comprehensively tested. Here, we measured the psychoacoustic sensitivity of a computational model optimized for everyday sound localization and recognition tasks. We used linear classifiers operating on the model's learned representations to estimate 1632 thresholds spanning the perceptual dimensions of sound. These model-derived thresholds closely matched thresholds measured behaviorally in humans on the same test battery. The results show that many classical psychophysical phenomena emerge from representations optimized for natural behavior and suggest that discrimination thresholds are determined by linear separability in these optimized representations, rather than intrinsic neural noise.

items.title: Psychedelics Restructure the Global Workspace of Consciousness
items.abstract_or_text: Psychoactive drugs profoundly alter consciousness, but the neural mechanisms by which they do so remain poorly understood. Global workspace theory may provide a framework for investigating these mechanisms. The global workspace, a candidate neural substrate of consciousness, is a set of brain regions that integrate and disseminate information to the rest of the brain. According to a recent model, the integrators, or 'gateways,' are characterized by synergistic interactions with other brain regions, while the disseminators, or 'broadcasters,' exhibit redundant interactions. Here, we measured the effects of various psychoactive drugs, including 'classic' psychedelics like LSD, mescaline, and psilocybin, 'atypical' psychedelics (entactogens) like MDMA, and the stimulant D-amphetamine, on the global workspace. In a secondary analysis of resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data on all these drugs, we found that classic psychedelics are associated with significant increases in the number of gateways in the frontoparietal control and dorsal attention networks. Meanwhile, MDMA and amphetamine reduced the number of gateways in the visual and somatomotor networks. The regional topographies of both synergy and redundancy distinguished classic psychedelics from other drugs. Finally, drugs producing similar changes in synergy and redundancy also produced similar profiles of subjective effects. Overall, our findings provide the first direct evidence that psychedelics may alter the synergistic and redundant interactions that characterize the global workspace of consciousness.

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Aquatic Ecotoxicity Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Aquatic ecosystems are threatened by thousands of chemicals whose hazard is often unknown. Laboratory tests of individual chemicals on individual species establish, for example, the Lethal Concentration for 50% of test individuals (LC50), but for most chemicals in use such data exist for only a small fraction of species. A growing body of research applies machine learning to bridge these gaps. Before such models can be relied on in regulatory and environmental management contexts, they must not only be accurate in general, but also quantify how far individual predictions can be trusted. We address this by training a Bayesian Factorization Machine (BFM) on ecotoxicity test data. The BFM matches the accuracy of the current state of the art in predicting LC50 values, and additionally quantifies the uncertainty of every prediction, separating the part arising from a lack of data (epistemic) from the part that is irreducible, reflecting inter-test and biological variability (aleatoric). We then show how this uncertainty propagates into environmental quality assessment: Species Sensitivity Distributions (SSDs) become ensembles of plausible curves rather than single fits, and the hazardous concentrations derived from them carry credible intervals that are widest for the data-poor chemicals where conventional SSDs are least reliable.

items.title: Developmental Convergence Across Diverse Genetic Architectures in Childhood Apraxia of Speech
items.abstract_or_text: Childhood apraxia of speech (CAS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder of speech-motor planning and programming, associated with literacy, academic, and psychosocial difficulties. We performed whole-exome sequencing in 11 families comprising 21 affected and 15 unaffected individuals with phenotyping spanning speech, language, cognition, literacy, and motor function. We identified 60 prioritized variant observations representing 22 unique variants across 20 genes with family-based segregation analysis assessed in informative relatives; 5 arose de novo. Our cohort included multiple affected siblings and extended relatives, with several families carrying multiple prioritized variants, suggesting cumulative or oligogenic susceptibility. Speech and literacy impairment co-occurred with oral-motor, feeding, and fine-motor difficulties. BrainSpan co-expression analysis identified MECP2 and ANK2 as the genes with the highest observed connectivity in the sampled postnatal network. Exploratory analysis of the KOLF2.1J perturbation atlas in undifferentiated human induced pluripotent stem cells identified a positive LMO3 expression-response score following NIPBL repression and opposing LMO3 and ANK2 response directions within a cohesin-associated perturbation cluster. These observations motivate testing in human neural cells. Functional enrichment, protein-association, and developmental-expression analyses supported shared biological themes involving chromatin regulation, neuronal signaling, and extracellular-matrix organization. Among six families, multiple affected relatives shared prioritized variants across a unique set of several genes, demonstrating multilocus candidate profiles whose individual and combined effects may contribute to CAS susceptibility. We propose four novel CAS candidate genes: LMO3 and PCDH10, previously linked to human accelerated regions, as well as MYCBP2 and PTPRS. Our work provides multiple testable hypotheses for future variant-specific functional validation in speech-motor development.

items.title: Coiled-coil homo-oligomerization and disaggregase Hsp104 act in parallel to stabilize orphan septins
items.abstract_or_text: Multiple septin family proteins co-assemble with strict subunit stoichiometry into hetero-oligomers. In the absence of native septin partners, purified septins aggregate in vitro, and "orphan" septins are found in pathological aggregates associated with neurodegenerative diseases. Cytosolic chaperones bind the septin GTPase domain to promote on-pathway septin folding but it was unclear how cells manage orphan septins to maintain subunit stoichiometry. Most septins have C-terminal domains (CTDs) that form heteromeric coiled coils within or between septin complexes. Here we present evidence that orphan yeast septins are protected from proteasomal degradation by forming transient coiled-coil homodimers and trimers and, in parallel, by the disaggregase chaperone Hsp104. Septins unable to undergo CTD-mediated homo-oligomerization require Hsp104 to accumulate to super-stoichiometric levels. We show that septin-encoding mRNAs differ in copy number per cell and subcellular localization, creating opportunities for transient subunit imbalances. These findings reveal a novel role for coiled coils and the proteostasis machinery in the fidelity of higher-order septin assembly.
